rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a blastocyst and acknowledges image limitations, but it overstates confidence in AA-level TE/ICM and hatching features that are not clearly demonstrable on this soft single image.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, endometrium, male factor diagnosis, BMI, first-cycle status, and day-5 development into prognosis and management.

Reasoning is logical and structured, with probability estimates tied to embryo quality and patient factors; minor tension exists between calling the image only intermediate-good while accepting the reported 4AA grade.

Recommendations are broadly evidence-based and consistent with IVF practice, especially support for single embryo transfer and avoiding unnecessary add-ons after one failure; minor overreach includes discussing PGT-A benefits somewhat broadly in a 27-year-old.

Provides clear practical next steps for current transfer and sensible future-cycle planning, including SET, transfer optimization, when not to overinvestigate, and male-factor review if repeated failure occurs.
